title: Drywall Touch-Up
short_answer: Fixing the wall itself, not the paint. Found before the painter it costs minutes; found after, it costs the repair plus a repainted wall.
summary: Fixing the wall itself, not the paint. Found before the painter it costs minutes; found after, it costs the repair plus a repainted wall.
plain_words: This is fixing the drywall — screw pops, dings, ridges you can see in a seam, fuzzy spots where somebody sanded through the paper. Walk the room with a bright light held flat against the wall; that's how you find them. Fill thin, feather it out wide, match the texture, and prime it before anybody paints over it.
when_to_use: Pre-paint QC walk finds drywall finish defects
Finisher punch pass after coats are done but before handoff to painter
prerequisites: Finish coats complete enough to judge surface quality
Bright work light for raking pass

tools.name: Low-tack tape or pencil for marking

steps.title: Raking light
steps.body: Take a bright work light and hold it close to the wall and nearly parallel to it, so the light rakes across the surface. Every high and low spot throws a shadow.

steps.title: One wall at a time
steps.body: Work one wall at a time, top to bottom. Sweeping a whole room at once misses things.

steps.title: Real viewing angle
steps.body: Also look from the angle and in the light the room is actually used in — a defect nobody can ever see from a normal standing position may not be worth chasing, and one under a wall-wash fixture absolutely is.

steps.title: Mark outside
steps.body: Mark outside the defect with low-tack tape or a light pencil dot. Never a marker on the wall — marker bleeds through primer and paint and becomes a second defect.

steps.title: Three buckets
steps.body: Sort what you mark into three buckets: drywall finish repair (this document), a real hole needing a patch (see Drywall Patch), and someone else's damage.

steps.title: Photo first
steps.body: Photograph other trades' damage before you touch it. Otherwise it silently becomes our cost.

steps.title: Batch work
steps.body: Then work in batches — all the cut-outs, all the fills, all the coats — rather than one defect start-to-finish at a time.

steps.title: Setting compound
steps.body: Setting compound for anything with depth — it sets chemically, so you can recoat the same visit instead of coming back tomorrow.

steps.title: Final coat
steps.body: Topping or lightweight for the final coat, even if the fill was hot mud. The last coat is the one you sand.

steps.title: Wider coats
steps.body: Thin coats, each one wider than the last. Same rule as everywhere else in finishing.

steps.title: Feather wide
steps.body: Feather much further than feels necessary. The repair fails at its edge, not its middle.

steps.title: Re-check
steps.body: Sand lightly and check again with the raking light before you call it done.

steps.title: Match texture
steps.body: Match the surrounding texture. A perfectly smooth repair in a textured wall is still an obvious repair.

steps.title: Prime every repair
steps.body: Prime every repair. Bare compound absorbs paint differently than the wall around it — this is the single handoff item that decides whether the painter's work shows.

steps.title: Full walk
steps.body: Raking-light walk done on every wall and ceiling, not just the ones somebody complained about.

steps.title: Repairs complete
steps.body: All repairs coated, sanded, textured to match, and primed.

steps.title: Cracks investigated
steps.body: Any crack investigated for cause, not just filled.

steps.title: Skim vs punch
steps.body: Any wall that needed a full skim identified and dealt with as finishing, not punch.

steps.title: Other trades
steps.body: Other trades' damage photographed and reported before repair.

steps.title: Clean up
steps.body: Tape and pencil marks removed. Floors cleaned of sanding dust.

steps.title: GC walk
steps.body: Walk it with the GC in the same light and get agreement before the painter starts.

warnings.title: Why this is its own step, before paint
warnings.body: A drywall defect found before the painter costs a knife, a little mud, and a dab of primer. The identical defect found after paint costs that same repair, plus priming, plus repainting the entire plane corner to corner — because a spot repaint on a finished wall flashes. One careful raking-light walk before the painter mobilizes is the cheapest hour in the finishing scope.

warnings.title: A crack is not a touch-up
warnings.body: Movement caused the crack — a missing or ineffective control joint, framing movement, or a joint landed on an opening corner. Filling a moving crack brings it back, usually within a season. Find the cause; see Hanging Drywall control joints. Do not treat it as punch fill.

warnings.title: A wall covered in defects is not punch work
warnings.body: If defects are everywhere on a wall, the finish never reached the specified level. That is a finishing problem — go back to Finishing Drywall and skim the plane properly. Chasing a hundred spots individually costs more than doing the wall.

experts.summary: Most defects are quick fixes; two are symptoms of something else. Screw or nail pop: reset the fastener or add one beside it holding the board tight, then two to three thin coats. Blister in tape: cut the blistered section out, re-bed that length properly — filling over a blister does not bond. Ridge down a seam: scrape or sand flat, skim wider and feather. Fuzzy patch from over-sanding: do not sand more — skim to seal raised fibers. Dings: fill and feather wide; broken paper = small patch. Shadow at butt joint: widen substantially — most commonly under-fixed defect. Dented corner bead: shallow dents fill; deep dent or kinked bead means replacing the bead. A crack means movement — stop, not a touch-up. Defects everywhere on a wall means the finish never hit spec — not punch work, skim the plane. The crack and bad-wall judgment calls are the valuable part of this page.

quality_checks.prompt: Raking-light walk on every wall and ceiling
Defects marked outside with tape or pencil — never marker
Every repair primed before painter handoff
Cracks investigated for cause — not filled as punch

common_mistakes.title: Defects found after paint
common_mistakes.wrong: Skip drywall punch and let the painter find defects
common_mistakes.why: Repair price doubles or worse once paint is on

common_mistakes.title: Not priming the repair
common_mistakes.wrong: Hand off bare compound to the painter
common_mistakes.why: Guarantees touch-up flashes and comes back to us

common_mistakes.title: Feathering too small
common_mistakes.wrong: Tight fill at the defect only
common_mistakes.right: Feather much further than feels necessary
common_mistakes.why: Repair fails at its edge — gets done twice

common_mistakes.title: Filling a crack
common_mistakes.wrong: Mud over a moving crack as punch work
common_mistakes.right: Stop and find the movement cause
common_mistakes.why: Warranty callback with our name on it

common_mistakes.title: Chasing spots on a bad wall
common_mistakes.wrong: Punch a hundred defects on a wall that needed skimming
common_mistakes.right: Identify and skim the plane as finishing
common_mistakes.why: More labor than doing the wall right

common_mistakes.title: Marker on the wall
common_mistakes.right: Low-tack tape or pencil outside the defect
common_mistakes.why: Marker bleeds through and becomes a new defect

common_mistakes.title: Sanding a fuzzy spot
common_mistakes.right: Skim to seal fibers, then light sand
common_mistakes.why: Each sanding pass makes it worse

common_mistakes.title: Undocumented other-trade damage
common_mistakes.wrong: Repair damage without photos or report

provenance.note: Defect causes and remedies follow standard finishing practice and manufacturer guidance on joint treatment and sanding. The raking-light inspection is how commercial drywall work is actually judged — the same check in Finishing Drywall, applied at punch. The prime-before-paint requirement traces to the same porosity mechanism documented in Paint Touch-Up. The crack-versus-touch-up and bad-wall-versus-punch distinctions are judgment calls reflecting GVC practice and the cost logic above, not a published standard.
